title: Sustained + Burst Profile Generator for Dedicated Capacity Soak and Autoscale Regression Detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Build a harness that synthesizes realistic sustained (steady-state) and short high-amplitude burst traffic profiles against Dedicated pools. The goal is to: 1) measure and baseline tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) under combinatorial profiles; 2) surface regressions in autoscaler behavior (scale-up latency, overshoot/oscillation) and serving runtime regressions; 3) provide deterministic CI checks and annotated dashboards for on-call and SRE use.

Key differentiators vs prior soak runs: the generator must support multi-phase scenarios (ramp -> steady -> short burst -> cooldown), configurable KV cache warmup, per-route token distributions, optional injection of slow downstreams to emulate underlying device variability, and automated regression detectors that compare current runs to a stored canonical baseline including signficance testing for p95 shifts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a configurable profile: ramp (0->target) over N minutes, sustain for M minutes, burst to Xx for B minutes, cool down; parameters passed via YAML/JSON.
Measure and store tokens/sec, per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), tail tokenization time, and KV cache hit rate for each interval at 10s resolution.
Regression detector flags when p95 increases >10% with p < 0.05 against the baseline or when sustained tokens/sec drops >8% for two consecutive windows.
CI job that runs a short smoke profile and fails the PR when a regression detector trip occurs; artifacts (raw traces, aggregated metrics, diffs) uploaded to the run artifact storage.
Grafana dashboard and a Prometheus metrics lineage for each run; charts include per-model tokens/sec, autoscaler actions (scale events, desired/actual replicas) and request queue lengths.
Support for running against Dedicated pools in staging and an offline mode that replays recorded traffic for deterministic comparison.
Documentation (design + runbook) in Confluence and a reproducible demo run recorded (screencast or CI artifact).
tasks: Design profile DSL and parameters (owner: Marco) - include KV warmup, prefix cache toggles, model variant selection.
Implement load generator plugin for multi-worker mode (k6-based prototype -> internal runner adapter).
Instrument autoscaler events into Prometheus (scale decision timestamp, policy used, observed latency signals).
Implement regression detection service: baseline storage, statistical comparison, and alert hooks.
Add CI integration: short smoke profile + artifact upload + PR check runner.
Create Grafana dashboard and notebook for automated run comparisons.
Run pilot on staging dedicated pool, iterate on thresholds, and record canonical baseline.
Write runbook for SRE: how to interpret regressions and rollback model/variant or change autoscaler policy.
progress_updates: 2026-02-15 — Kickoff: agreed DSL shape (ramp/steady/burst/cooldown) and minimal set of metrics. Decided to prototype with k6 to validate concurrency semantics.
2026-02-22 — Prototype: k6-based runner can achieve target tokens/sec but struggled with proper KV cache warmup across workers; added per-worker warmup phase to the DSL.
2026-03-01 — Instrumentation: autoscaler now emits scale decision events (policy, desired_replicas) to Prometheus metrics. Initial dashboard draft created.
2026-03-05 — Statistical model: implemented a two-sample bootstrap comparator for p95 with configurable alpha; initial thresholds calibrated against 5 historical runs.
2026-03-10 — CI: short smoke job implemented; flagged a false-positive run due to un-warmed caches. Decided to include deterministic warmup in CI profiles to reduce noise.
2026-03-12 — Pilot: ran 2-hour steady + 30s burst on staging dedicated pool; observed a 12% p95 increase during burst for one model variant and an autoscaler lag of ~45s. Triage scheduled.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): Prefer statistical tests over static thresholds for p95; runtime signals can be spiky. Marco to prototype bootstrap approach.
Jinsoo Park (SRE) (2026-02-24): KV warmup across workers will need coordinated prefixes or a shared warm cache marker; otherwise CI will be flaky. Suggest 'shared-warm' toggle.
Design review (2026-03-02): PM asked to include customer-impact tags on runs to prioritize regression triage. Added 'customer_impact' metadata to runs.

Marco Chen (2026-03-11): Pilot showed autoscaler cooldown default of 60s causes underprovision during burst; proposed policy changes: shorten scale-up cooldown to 20s for dedicated pools on burst policy.
Rationale note (2026-03-12): We will keep both conservative sustained-policy and aggressive-burst-policy to avoid oscillation; regression detector will be policy-aware when comparing runs.
